trusted_publishers.rationale: Paho Lurie-Gregg maintains typenum, the type-level arithmetic library used by generic-array. Accept the verified release from its upstream maintainer; this is publisher trust, not completion of the earlier deferred source review.

Official wasm-bindgen repository release identity for its Rust/JavaScript bindings and procedural generators. Trust this project release rather than attributing the workflow to historical human uploader alexcrichton.
David Rheinsberg maintains r-efi, the Rust definitions of the UEFI reference specification. Trust his verified release of this platform binding package.

Official smallvec repository release identity for the small-vector implementation used by Rust/Servo infrastructure. Accept project release responsibility for its unsafe storage implementation; no local source certification is claimed.
Frank Denis maintains the SipHash implementation in jedisct1/rust-siphash. Trust this verified release from the cryptographic-library maintainer; this is not a local cryptographic review.
Zeeshan Ali Khan maintains zbus and zvariant and publishes smol synchronization/channel packages. Trust the verified releases of these specific D-Bus and async infrastructure packages.
John Nunley maintains smol async infrastructure. Trust his verified concurrent-queue, futures-lite and piper releases from the smol-rs repositories.

Daniel Alley maintains the quick-xml parser in tafia/quick-xml. Accept responsibility of the verified upstream release publisher for this local fuzz dependency, without claiming production XML parser security.
Official Google zerocopy repository release identity for the layout/conversion library and its derive macros. Trust project release responsibility; unsafe correctness is not locally audited.
Martin Kroening publishes the Hermit Rust platform ABI from hermit-os/hermit-rs. Trust this verified release of the platform interface maintained with the Hermit project.

Alex Gaynor publishes the rust-openssl bindings from rust-openssl/rust-openssl. Trust these verified releases of OpenSSL binding/build infrastructure; system/native OpenSSL remains part of the trusted toolchain.

Yuki Okushi publishes Rust PHF lookup tables and generators. The existing pinned Mozilla audit set also explicitly trusts user-id 51017 for these same packages; accept direct, narrower local trust after checking the actual locked publications.
Official Rust Random rand repository release identity. Trust this project release for local test random generation, without claiming an independent RNG or cryptographic audit.
Hayden Stainsby publishes tracing and tracing-attributes from the Tokio tracing project. Trust these verified instrumentation and procedural-macro releases.
Jonas Platte publishes axum-core from the Tokio axum repository. Trust this verified release of its HTTP request/response abstraction layer.
The diwic account maintains dbus-rs and publishes libdbus-sys. Trust this verified release of the native D-Bus binding/build package; native libdbus/toolchain is not independently audited here.
SteveLauC published the exact nix 0.29.0 release from nix-rust/nix. Trust this historical release of the project Unix API bindings; current ownership is not used as publication evidence.
Kornel maintains rust-security-framework and publishes the Apple Security framework wrappers and bindings. Trust only the verified historical releases of these named packages.

Official sqlcipher-src repository release identity. Explicitly accept this maintainer's release responsibility for the SQLCipher/libtomcrypt source bundle described by its pinned README and manifest. This is new, package-specific trust in the bundler, not an independent review of bundled C, cryptography or release workflow.
Simon Sapin publishes Servo string interning/code generation and html5ever. Trust these verified releases from their Servo repositories; this does not certify production HTML parser behavior.
Kathryn Long maintains widestring-rs and publishes the UTF-16/UTF-32 FFI string library. Trust this verified project release, including its unsafe string representation code.
Jeff Muizelaar published the exact core-foundation 0.9.4 release from the Servo platform-bindings repository. Trust this historical Apple Core Foundation wrapper release.
Josh Bowman-Matthews publishes Servo platform bindings and html5ever support crates. Trust the verified core-foundation, web_atoms and markup5ever releases from the listed repositories.

Jelte Fennema-Nio maintains derive_more and derive_more-impl. The existing pinned Mozilla set explicitly trusts the same user-id for these packages and describes his PR security review; accept narrower historical local trust.

The kotauskas account maintains interprocess, whose pinned manifest, README and published source commit describe the local IPC toolkit. Explicitly trust this verified project release for its Unix/Windows IPC implementation; no local unsafe/ACL correctness certification is claimed.

Nico Goh maintains sqlite-wasm-rs and its rsqlite-vfs package. Explicitly trust these verified project releases and their SQLite/Wasm host-binding build integration; bundled C and VFS isolation are not independently audited.
Martin Robinson publishes the Servo tendril string container from servo/html5ever. Trust this verified project release of the parser support library.

Daniel Brotsky publishes keyring and dbus-secret-service; the project README documents the synchronous Secret Service backend and keyring integration. Trust these verified project releases, including their documented access to the OS credential store when called.

The gwenn account publishes rusqlite and libsqlite3-sys from rusqlite/rusqlite. Trust these verified project releases of SQLite wrappers and native build integration; this does not independently certify SQLite or SQLCipher C.
The Noratrieb account publishes rustc-hash from the official rust-lang repository. Trust this verified release of the compiler hash implementation; it is explicitly non-cryptographic.

Oriol Brufau publishes selectors and servo_arc from the Servo Stylo repository. Trust these verified project releases of browser CSS and shared-allocation infrastructure; the recently created registry account is verified by exact historical publication, not an old account assumption.

Folkert de Vries publishes zlib-rs from the Trifecta Tech Foundation repository. Trust this verified project release of the Rust compression implementation; no local decompressor robustness audit is claimed.
Official rust-crc32fast repository release identity for CRC32 dispatch/implementation. Trust this verified project release for local test execution.
Alan Somers publishes nix from nix-rust/nix. Trust the verified nix 0.32.0 project release of Unix platform API wrappers.
Chip Senkbeil maintains typed-path, a lexical Unix/Windows path library. Trust this verified upstream release; no security claim about callers using paths for filesystem authorization is made.

Official zip-rs/zip2 repository release identity for the ZIP reader/writer. Trust this verified project release for local synthetic fuzz inputs; this does not independently certify archive extraction on hostile production input.

import_candidates_not_added.name: ariel-os
import_candidates_not_added.reason: Historical futures-lite delta chain; chosen direct trust in the exact verified notgull publication already covers that package. No additional import adopted.

new_agent_audits.name: enumflags2_derive
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and the complete procedural macro implementation. It parses attribute arguments and enum syntax with syn, accepts only explicit unsigned fixed-width repr types and unit variants, validates literal powers of two/ranges, defers nonliteral checks to generated constants and infers remaining bits. Generated impls use the enumflags2 API, integer casts, flag unions and trait implementations; the unsafe RawBitFlags impl assumes the compiler-checked enum layout. Input expressions remain caller Rust syntax and are not executed by the macro. Work and allocations scale with supplied syntax. No build script, native code, filesystem/environment/network/process access, constructors or autonomous tasks. This is not a proof of macro hygiene or arbitrary caller unsafe implementations.

new_agent_audits.name: redox_syscall
new_agent_audits.notes: Reviewed both manifests, module inventory, all four architecture syscall/assembly definitions, call.rs syscall wrappers, data/flag/error and schemev2 representations, directory-entry parsing/writing, MMIO/PIO and signal atomic implementations, plus the Scheme dispatch path and seek helpers. Constant/error tables were inspected as declarative data; the mutable/blocking Scheme variants were inventoried as dispatch variants, not fully reviewed or separately proved. Expected authority is explicit caller-requested Redox syscalls, caller-provided kernel packet pointers and mapped device/port I/O; none executes on linking or initialization. The crate has no build script, installer, hidden endpoint, ambient scanning or background work. This limited safe-to-run review assumes intended Redox ABI/privileged callers and trusted packet addresses, not arbitrary packet fuzzing through Scheme::handle. Raw byte views/padding, a temporary bits() byte view in PtraceFlags, malformed DirentIter records, signal indexing and atomic ordering are not certified sound or robust; malformed directory lengths can panic and raw packet pointers can be unsafe. Redox-specific dependency paths are not exercised on the Windows/Linux/macOS fuzz hosts. No claim of safe-to-deploy, kernel/driver security or portability of invoking Redox syscalls on another OS.

new_agent_audits.name: enumflags2
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and production modules const_api, fallible, formatting, iter and lib, including serde and macro-generated integer implementations. The representation stores a numeric flag mask with PhantomData; checked conversion masks with ALL_BITS and rejects unknown bits. Iteration extracts the lowest bit, clears it and terminates within the primitive bit width. Unsafe transmute_copy depends on the RawBitFlags contract and matching enum repr generated by the companion macro; unchecked constructors retain their caller obligations. Serialization/formatting and collection operations use caller-provided traits only. No build script/native code, ambient I/O, environment reads, process launches or autonomous tasks. Generic user iterators/traits may perform arbitrary caller-defined work; this is not a proof of all layout/serde correctness.

new_agent_audits.name: blocking
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and the complete library state machine, pool scheduling, thread creation, Unblock read/write/seek/stream adapters and cancellation transitions. Expected authority is running caller-submitted closures and caller-supplied I/O on lazily spawned blocking-N threads; there is no task until requested. The BLOCKING_MAX_THREADS environment setting is parsed and clamped to 1..10000, default 500; the explicit setter accepts a caller-chosen nonzero limit. Idle workers use a condvar timeout. Adapter buffers default to 8 MiB for I/O or 8192 stream items, with caller override; queues and submitted work are not globally bounded. No own file/socket opens, subprocesses, downloads or build script. Unsafe code is forbidden. Caller closures can block forever or exhaust resources, and cancellation cannot forcibly stop arbitrary blocking I/O; this safe-to-run decision assumes controlled local harness work, not an untrusted task sandbox.

new_agent_audits.name: async-recursion
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all three production macro modules. The attribute validates async function syntax and at most two distinct ?Send/Sync arguments, visits reference/generic lifetimes and rewrites the signature to Pin<Box<dyn Future>> and body to Box::pin(async move ...). Caller syntax is quoted into generated Rust and is not interpreted/executed by the macro; lifetimes and trait bounds are compiler checked. No own unsafe blocks, build script/native code, file/environment/socket/process APIs or background work. Runtime recursion/allocations belong to the annotated caller function and can exhaust resources; no general recursion bound or production macro correctness certification is claimed.

new_agent_audits.name: doctest-file
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all four production modules, including argument/string parsing, anchor/hidden-line processing and token construction. Expected compile-time authority is reading CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and opening the filename explicitly supplied by trusted Rust source (absolute paths and parent traversal are accepted). BufReader lines are converted to an escaped proc_macro Literal::string; file contents do not become macro executable code. The resulting documentation may be used by rustdoc as caller-authorized doctests. No write, process, network, install, build script or unsafe code. Files/line lengths are not capped, so compile-time source arguments and repository fixtures must be trusted and finite; this is not an isolation boundary for hostile macro invocations.

new_agent_audits.name: matchit
new_agent_audits.notes: Reviewed both manifests and the router, radix-tree insertion/removal/matching, route escaping and parameter storage/remapping paths. No runtime dependencies, build script, generated/native code or ambient I/O. All routing work operates on supplied strings, node vectors and caller values. UnsafeCell is used to share matching logic between immutable and exclusive mutable Router methods; unsafe Send/Sync are bounded on T. Traversal consumes prefixes or backtracks through an explicit stack; registration rejects malformed wildcard syntax and panics above its parameter-name limit. Formatting may call caller value traits. This safe-to-run review does not prove all aliasing invariants or production route-parser/DoS correctness.

new_agent_audits.name: ordered-stream
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all four production modules: stream/future traits, map/filter/then/peek adapters, two-way join and multi-stream polling. no_std code delegates only to caller-provided stream/future/comparison/closure implementations, using pin-project-lite for structural pinning. Join holds at most one buffered item per side and multi-join scans supplied streams with at most one additional tighter-bound pass. Filter loops may consume indefinitely ready caller streams; callers must bound their workload. No own executable unsafe block, build script, native code, filesystem, environment, network, threads, process launch or autonomous task. This does not certify arbitrary underlying streams, ordering correctness or starvation resistance.

new_agent_audits.name: recvmsg
new_agent_audits.notes: Reviewed manifests and module inventory, buffer ownership/growth/initialization/cursor and Drop paths, Unix recvmsg and Windows recv/recvfrom implementations, address wrapping and synchronous/asynchronous retry/peek/discard adapters. Other forwarding modules and trait extension inventories were checked for additional authority; this was a focused safe-to-run review, not a proof of every unsafe block. Expected authority is receiving or discarding messages on a caller-supplied socket/descriptor and invoking caller buffer growth/receiver implementations. No socket is independently connected to an external endpoint; no own build script, process launch, filesystem enumeration, installer or background thread. Buffer quotas are optional; absent a caller quota, growth and retry on changing/oversized messages may exhaust memory or stall. Raw ownership, OS sockaddr layouts, initialization contracts, trait behavior and concurrent-reader races remain outside a production-safety claim. This review does not run network integration tests or certify an IPC isolation boundary.

new_agent_audits.name: uds_windows
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and the five production source files, including address conversion, AF_UNIX connect/bind/listen/accept, socket ownership/options, WinSock startup and overlapped extension lookup. Expected authority is local socket I/O requested by callers. UnixStream::pair explicitly creates a tempfile directory/socket and a helper thread, then joins it; the endpoint is local and temporary. Other operations use caller-supplied paths/sockets; NUL/overlong outbound paths are rejected. WSAIoctl obtains fixed WinSock extension GUID function pointers, with no arbitrary DLL loading or code downloads. No build script, process launch, registry modification, remote endpoint selection or constructor-time work. Unsafe overlapped lifetimes, raw OS address lengths/UTF-8 assumptions, buffer-size narrowing and all FFI soundness are not certified; this is safe-to-run in controlled use, not safe-to-deploy or an ACL/isolation review.

new_agent_audits.name: dtoa-short
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and the complete library implementation. no_std code formats caller-supplied floating values through dtoa into a fixed stack scratch buffer, adjusts decimal/scientific precision using bounded slice loops, and writes only to caller fmt::Write. The unsafe copy assumes dtoa formatted output fits its buffer representation; the extra byte permits carry/sign adjustment. The unchecked UTF-8 conversion is of ASCII formatting bytes. Nonfinite values and arbitrary implementations of the public dtoa::Float/Floating traits are not certified; this is not a numeric-correctness or all-unsafe-contract proof. No build script/native code, file/environment/network/process access or background work.

new_agent_audits.name: secret-service
new_agent_audits.notes: Reviewed manifests, module inventory, async collection/item APIs, blocking connection and prompt paths, proxy declarations/destinations, DH/HKDF/AES session handling and common lock/unlock/secret formatting utilities. Expected authority is explicitly connecting to the configured session D-Bus and accessing org.freedesktop.secrets on request, including caller-requested creation/deletion/locking/unlocking and desktop prompts. No own external HTTP endpoint, file scan, subprocess, build script, installer or initialization-time credential access. Session entropy comes from OsRng; loops use caller/service data and a fixed-size DH private exponent. Trust the session bus environment and service; malformed responses, cryptographic parameters/timing/key zeroization, unbounded service data and waiting for a prompt are not production-certified. Blocking item/collection wrappers were inventoried as counterparts, not independently proved. Upstream integration tests can modify OS Secret Service test entries and were not run; this audit covers controlled harness build/use, not running those tests against a real credential store.

new_agent_audits.name: constant_time_eq
new_agent_audits.notes: Read manifests, complete build script and production generic/SSE2/NEON/DIT modules. Build code reads Cargo target architecture and a test opt-in, then emits fixed cfg lines; no downloads, subprocesses or file writes. Runtime compares supplied byte slices/arrays using length checks and bounded scalar/SIMD loads. Inline assembly performs register comparisons/masks, optimizer barriers and, on feature-detected AArch64, temporary thread DIT state changes restored by a Drop guard; no OS reconfiguration or privileged I/O. CPU feature overrides are unsafe caller APIs. No filesystem/network/process authority or autonomous work. This safe-to-run review does not certify constant-time behavior on every compiler/CPU, mathematical correctness or all instruction/unsafe contracts; instruction-count tests were not run.

new_agent_audits.name: ego-tree
new_agent_audits.notes: Read manifests and all five production modules, including node ID conversion, Vec storage and unchecked indexing, mutation/detach/reparent/clone paths, axis/depth traversal, display/sorting and optional serde reconstruction. no_std plus alloc code has no build script, native code or ambient I/O. Work operates only on supplied values, tree IDs and caller callbacks/serializers. Root/index assumptions and valid tree links underpin unsafe indexing; foreign IDs, pathological caller mutations/cycles and deeply recursive serde trees are not certified sound or resource-bounded. In particular recursive serialization/reconstruction may exhaust stack on deep input. This scoped safe-to-run audit is not a proof of all graph invariants or a production hostile-tree safety claim.

new_agent_audits.name: scraper
new_agent_audits.notes: Read manifests, production HTML tree sink/parse/select paths, DOM/node and element adapters, CSS selector/serde integration, serializers and CLI main. Library operations consume supplied HTML/CSS and construct/query an ego-tree; script nodes and processing instructions stay data, and serialization does not execute JavaScript. No library network connection, file read, subprocess or build script. The optional CLI explicitly reads stdin or argument-named files and prints results; its --install-man-page PATH option creates PATH/man1 and writes the bundled scraper.1 only when requested. That documented installation option was inspected, not executed. Input/tree/selector work has no global memory/time bound; recursion, selector behavior and upstream unsafe crates are not production-certified. No claim that serialized HTML is sanitized for browser execution.

new_trust_summary.date_semantics: One UTC day per package/publication, start inclusive and end exclusive. Distinct release dates are not merged.
new_trust_summary.risk: New direct, package-specific publisher trust. Verified provenance is not an independent source, workflow, native C/ASM, cryptographic or production-safety audit; individual decisions and special native/IPC trust are explicit above.

new_audit_summary.method: Prioritize remaining reverse-dependency fanout. Focused source reviews of build/runtime authority and generated behavior; not a proof of every unsafe block. Exact reviewed paths and limitations are in each audit note. File integrity inventories are byte-comparison evidence, not a claim that every listed file was manually reviewed.

source_review_prioritization.method: Baseline remaining sorted by descending transitive_users from the previous all-features dump-graph; after publisher coverage, audits recorded in that order.
source_review_prioritization.graph_command: cargo vet dump-graph --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --store-path supply-chain/fuzz --locked --frozen --output-format json
source_review_prioritization.graph_provenance: Fanout counts and graph hash retained from review-2026-11-26-continuation.json; manifests and dependency locks are unchanged. Not a claim that dump-graph was rerun in this worktree.

rust_tests.prepared_environment: Reused existing Strawberry Perl 5.40.5.1 and libclang 18.1.1 under main checkout target/tools, read-only; archive SHA-256 checked against scripts/bootstrap-{perl,libclang}.ps1. Dot-sourced scripts/build-env.ps1 for CMake. Workspace tests passed using the worktree target. Clippy then started a duplicate native build; that validation process tree was stopped and clippy/leak tests rerun with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Projects/NymWrap/target to reuse the existing build cache. Commands still use this worktree manifests/sources; main/worktree Cargo.lock SHA-256 equality checked. Only generated build-cache outputs are shared; no system installation, native-version change, store/lock edit or tracked tooling change.

validation.ci: Not run; local validation only. M6 and other dependency graph gates are outside this task.

limitations: Local Windows gate success does not close CI or M6.
safe-to-run only; no new safe-to-deploy audit, dependency version change, exemption or wildcard audit.
Do not interpret focused source reviews or publisher trust as independent human review of production parsing, cryptography, native code, unsafe contracts or IPC isolation.
Upstream crate tests touching a real OS credential store were not run; Secret Service use assumes the controlled harness and trusted session bus.
Archived version sources and registry response hashes are durable review identifiers; full fetched responses/logs remain untracked under target/vet/fuzz-task9/completion.
